messages:
Maria: heads-up - since 06:10 UTC we saw a pile of 1-GPU pods pending in us-west2, backlog up 3x
Tariq: which nodegroups?
Maria: gpu-small-2 and gpu-micro-1, mostly tiny training jobs from a single customer
Sam: logs show a lot of preemptions + nic egress saturation on racks with mixed pods. when NIC hits ~95% the scheduler starts reshuffling and evicting small pods
Jen: is this the same churn we saw last month or a new pattern?
Maria: similar surface but different trigger. last month was kubelet heartbeat flaps; today it's network egress + fractional gang preempting bigger gpu jobs -> chain reaction
Tariq: can you paste a scheduler log snippet?
Maria: sure: ```I0310 06:12:07.123456       1 scheduler_binder.go:214] Pod gpu-job-42 preempted due to resource reclaim: tiny-pod occupying fractional slot```
Sam: Ugh. fractional small pods spread across nodes are preventing decent binpacking. when nic saturates one node the autoscaler moves pods and we get preempt loop :weary:
Jen: short-term: can we throttle egress per gpu node class or move small pods to a dedicated pool?
Tariq: we have warm-pools for latency but they’re heterogeneous. proposal: create a pinned 'micro-gpu' pool with strict nodeSelector + network QoS, and migrate tiny-pod workloads there
Maria: +1. Also suggest an admission limit: max 2 concurrent tiny pods per rack until we rebalance. simple admission webhook could do that quickly
Sam: ops-bot: roll up current pending counts?
ops-bot: us-west2: pending tiny-gpu pods: 124; affected nodegroups: gpu-small-2(78), gpu-micro-1(46)
Jen: medium-term: consider a scheduler predicate change to prefer co-locating tiny pods on fewer nodes (binpack tiny first) so big jobs can find contiguous slots
Tariq: we could also tweak preempt windows: increase grace window to avoid thrash when network blips cause temporary saturation
Maria: another idea: enable a tiny-pod eviction-cost label so descheduler can avoid evicting pods with small work remaining, prevents repeating restarts
Sam: cost note: current churn is adding ~12% GPU-hours due to reschedules. if we pigeonhole tiny jobs into a cheaper burst pool we cut that tail cost
Jen: action items: 1) create micro-gpu pinned pool + migrate best-effort tiny workloads (Tariq) 2) deploy admission webhook limiting per-rack tiny pod concurrency (Maria) 3) tweak preempt grace window and add eviction-cost label (Sam) 4) monitor pending count and NIC egress per-rack (Jen)
Tariq: assigning 1/2 to me, 3 to Sam, 2 to Maria, 4 to Jen. I'll draft the pool spec now
Maria: thanks — I'll prototype the webhook script (fast) and share a patch
Sam: I'll run a canary with 10% traffic to micro-pool after pool created
Jen: ping when you have the pool spec and I’ll add dashboards for NIC egress + pending backlog
Maria: FYI sample pool nodeSelector: ```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Node
metadata:
  labels:
    gpu.size: micro
    gpu.qos: burst
``` 
Tariq: timeline: try to have micro-pool and webhook in staging by EOD today, prod rollout tomorrow if green
Sam: noted. will also add a short-lived k8s-descheduler job to consolidate tiny pods overnight as quick mitigation
Jen: thanks team. keep notes here and tag oncall if eviction rate spikes > 10/min
Maria: tagging @oncall for awareness. :thumbsup:
